deep.reconstruction:
The page has no text. It holds pencil and coloured-ink sketches drawn on the back of a fan-fold IBM System/370 job-accounting printout; the printout text shows through in mirror image. Read with the series (cote 154, 'système de pseudo-droites') and the next page, the sketches seem to be exploratory pictures of pseudo-line configurations and of their deformations.

(1) Upper middle and right: chains of lens-shaped regions. These are two curves through common marked points bounding digons. They are probably either pictures of what is forbidden in a pseudo-line system (two pseudo-lines meeting twice) or of how a configuration degenerates when two crossings are pushed together and annihilated.

(2) Middle row: points of high multiplicity. These are marked points through which three to five lines pass (stars), strung along one horizontal red-ink line. This is the 'critical relative position' (position relative critique) situation that the next page indexes as vertices ρ of the cellular complex X* = Bal(Σ).

(3) Centre: a bundle of lines through a highlighted red point. Dashed red, green and black lines run parallel to one line of the bundle, and nearby triple points are blackened as small triangles. This looks like a study of perturbing (translating) one line of a critical configuration to the left or right. Such a move produces nearby stable or substable positions, i.e. the edges a_{s,ω} leaving a vertex ρ, which the next page describes as 'generalisation of D_{s,ω} at s to the left vs. to the right'.

(4) Right: a small quadrilateral of four marked points on two lines, inside an oval. This is possibly a cell or face of the complex of relative positions, or a local picture of a quadrilateral face around an edge a_L.

(5) Bottom: isolated segments with marked endpoints. These are possibly pictures of an edge with its two incident vertices, matching the next page's 'saisir les deux sommets incidents à a_L'.

Overall, the page serves the project of describing the local structure of the cell complex of relative positions of a pseudo-line, or a moving line, with respect to a fixed system Σ. Its vertices are critical positions, its edges substable positions and its faces stable positions. That is the setting of oriented-matroid / pseudoline-arrangement flip graphs and of the mutation (triangle-flip) structure.
errors: No textual claims to check. The digon pictures, if meant as pseudo-line arrangements, would violate the 'cross exactly once' axiom; most likely they are deliberate illustrations of degenerate or forbidden situations rather than errors.

ideas.what: Perturbing a critical (multiple-point) position of a line relative to a system of pseudo-lines into neighbouring stable or substable positions, left or right
ideas.modern_name: Local structure of the space of one-element extensions / flip (mutation) graph of pseudoline arrangements; cell complex of extensions of an oriented matroid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956, triangle flips); Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, 1980s); Las Vergnas, Bland, Björner et al. (oriented matroid extension spaces)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; the pseudo-line notes are only in the Montpellier archive (cote 154)

ideas.what: Digon or lens pictures of two curves meeting twice
ideas.modern_name: Digon elimination / bigon removal in curve arrangements (forbidden in pseudoline arrangements)

missed.claim: Historical detail only: Grothendieck drafted these 1983–84 pseudo-line notes on recycled computing-centre printout dated 1982 (Julian date 82.231, i.e. 19 August 1982, IBM 370 under MVS/VS2). This suggests he used scrap paper, probably from the Montpellier university computing centre. It is of no mathematical consequence.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor help for dating and contextualising the manuscript sheets; not mathematical.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only exploratory sketches with no text. They plausibly illustrate the critical, substable and stable position analysis developed on the next page, which matches known pseudoline / oriented-matroid flip structures. There is nothing independently new.
transcription_corrections: The page number '149' is handwritten in the bottom-left corner.
The printout date 82.231 is a Julian date (19 Aug 1982).
The central bundle includes lines in red, green and black dashed ink, plus a red ink point at the centre and a long red ink horizontal line in the middle row.
Several triple points near the central bundle are blackened as small triangles, not just dots.
